description.html: The fishing boat wreck shows an old wooden boat with a cabin on deck, round portholes, rope details and worn planks. The boat leans slightly and sits on a base with colorful coral details, and there is an opening in the hull that fish can swim into. Unlike pirate ships, it has no masts or sails, so the wreck looks calmer and more realistic.

Fish happily use it as a hiding place, and the darker space inside the hull especially suits shy species and fish that hide during the day. The wreck combines well with an anchor, stones and plants and gives the aquarium a nautical theme without too many colors.

Before placing it, rinse the wreck in lukewarm water, without soap. Set it on a flat part of the bottom and press the base lightly into the sand or gravel so it stands firmly. Turn the opening sideways or toward the front glass so you can see fish going in and out. When algae builds up on the surface, take it out and clean it with a soft brush under running water.
